messages:
alex: FYI customer on enterprise tier reporting streaming responses cut off mid-token, then client reconnects and gets 502 + repeated chunks. They say this started after upgrading to redwood-js v1.8.0. Full repro attached below.

maria: ack, can you paste the minimal repro and any request ids?

alex: here's the simplified Node repro they sent. note they use EventSource polyfill in Node and a custom reconnect backoff:```js
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('chunk', e.data);
es.onerror = (err) => { console.log('es error', err); es.close(); /* reconnect after backoff */ };
// They also call fetch('/client/heartbeat') every 10s to keep connection alive
```

sam: logs from their side (sanitized):
```
[2024-09-01T14:02:12.123Z] recv chunk: "Hello, wor"
[2024-09-01T14:02:12.456Z] socket closed: ECONNRESET
[2024-09-01T14:02:12.789Z] reconnect attempt 1
[2024-09-01T14:02:13.012Z] POST /v1/streams?model=redwood-large 502 Bad Gateway (X-Req-Id: req_customer_7f3)
[2024-09-01T14:02:13.045Z] server sent duplicate chunk: "ld!"
```

jun: interesting that 502 happens only on reconnect. Could be routing to a warm node that hasn't loaded KV cache, or a transient gateway oom. Also customer says they saw 429 shortly before 502 in some runs.

maria: ops-bot created incident; can eng-runtime triage? we need to know if this can cause double charging when client replays partial chunks. customer claims they were billed for both original + reconnect.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-3114. Assigned to eng-runtime. Ticket: https://redwood-internal/t/INC-2024-3114

eng-runtime: looking. two quick asks: do we have the full request id(s) from headers? alex, can you paste X-Req-Id from the 502 and the prior stream request? also, does the SDK include a streaming resume token on reconnect (it shouldn't for SSE)?

alex: they captured headers. First stream request had X-Req-Id: req_customer_7f3. Reconnect request X-Req-Id: req_customer_7f3-replay (their client reuses a trace id locally). Response headers on reconnect: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`, `X-Server-Node: gw-12`, `X-Upstream-Error: connection_reset`.

eng-runtime: thanks. quick hypothesis: reconnect attempts that happen before the original connection finished can hit our gateway rate limiter if multiple requests from same customer come in quickly. If gateway returns 502 we might still be streaming partial frames back to client; client reconnection then picks up a new partial response from a different backend that repeats final tokens. Need to confirm whether token accounting occurs on first-stream-close or on final frame ack. cc @jun

jun: accounting currently marks tokens as billed at emission time by the serving node. If backend A emitted final chunk and then later gateway error occurred, customer could see charged tokens even if client didn't receive the final frame. Reconnect to backend B may re-emit trailing tokens — that explains duplicate content + billing.

maria: customer wants mitigation ASAP. short-term options? force single in-flight stream per session id? increase gateway retry-backoff? send a 5xx that indicates non-idempotent so SDK avoids immediate replay?

sam: implement change in SDK to avoid automatic immediate reconnects for 5xx/502 on newer versions. We can push a patch to redwood-js to not auto-replay streams if the error code is 5xx and the previous connection had partial payload. But we need reliable detection of "partial payload" on client side.

alex: customer is on a patched app now reusing old SDK; they're seeing duplicates with node eventsource polyfill. They can reproduce locally with a simple script that force-closes socket mid-stream.

eng-runtime: for the server side: add a short window (2s) where gateway holds off charging if it returns upstream 502 and the upstream indicated `connection_reset` before final frame. That is a bit invasive but feasible as a short-term mitigation for enterprise accounts. Longer term we should change accounting semantics to finalize billing only when we fully flush/ack the final frame or when underlying runtime confirms completion.

jun: agree. I'll open a design doc. For immediate triage I'll instrument the gateway to log `stream_id -> emit_state` and add a small rollback in billing if we detect upstream fail-without-final-frame and a subsequent replay within 5s.

maria: can support get a simple workaround for the customer to reduce impact? e.g., disable automatic replay in their client until we push fixes?

alex: yes i told them to set their reconnect backoff to >=3s and to treat 5xx as terminal for streaming (i.e., surface error to app instead of auto-reopening). they accepted temporary change.

eng-runtime: note for repro we should try two cases: 1) client reconnects immediately (<200ms) 2) delayed reconnect (2-5s). also try with SDKs: redwood-js v1.8.0, redwood-js v1.7.2, and redwood-python v0.13.5. If only v1.8.0 auto-replays aggressively, patching lib may be quicker.

sam: I'll open a pr to redwood-js to add a config `streamAutoReplay: falseByDefaultAfter502` and ship a patch release.

alex: customer asked about billing refund scope. finance says we can do manual refund for duplicate tokens once we have X-Req-Id list. I'll collect the request ids and billing timestamps and attach to INC-2024-3114.

maria: thanks all. eng-runtime, please post follow-up when you have logs and tentative ETA for gateway rollback. sam, please link pr to the incident.

eng-runtime: will update in ~3h after initial logs. preliminary finding: gateway ratelimit + upstream connection reset triggers a path that does not send final delimiter; working on a fix.

alex: customer updated: with reconnect backoff increased they stopped seeing duplicates after ~20 minutes of testing. they're still asking for a guarantee though.

ops-bot: INC-2024-3114 status changed -> investigating :mag_right:
